question: Is the 0.30 BiG-SCAPE cutoff too low, and would an 8 kb antiSMASH neighbourhood have covered the pantaphos cluster?
answer: No to both, and the two questions turn out to be one. 10 kb is the smallest integer neighbourhood that keeps the whole pantaphos cassette -- the worst member needs 9,792 bp, so 8 kb and 9 kb both clip the terminal ATP-grasp in every member. But a ~10 kb flank is also 79% of the domains BiG-SCAPE compares, and it is what splits one chemistry into several families by host species. The cutoff cannot fix that: swept over 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.40 the largest family stays 186 at every value and the two families whose representatives are 0.020 apart never merge. Affinity propagation is the splitter, not the threshold.
method: big_scape.network.families.generate_families was called unchanged against a copy of the finished GenBank Enterobacterales database, so this is the real affinity-propagation step with the real parameters (damping 0.90, max_iter 1000, convergence_iter 200, PREFERENCE 0.0, DENSITY 0.85, DENSE_PREFERENCE -5.0). Only connected-component assembly and persistence are local, because the CLI path insists on a Pfam HMM it does not need once every CDS is already scanned -- and the Pfam database lives on an external drive that was disconnected. Script: recluster.py. All 1,088,550 stored comparisons were reused; nothing was re-scanned or re-compared.

validation.replication_at_0.30: 112 families, largest 186, 43 singletons -- identical to the production run's headline figures
validation.components: 30 multi-node connected components + 43 singletons = the 73 rows in the production connected_component table
validation.note: The same 2 that docs/comparisons/bigscape_reproducibility/ found oscillating between identical BiG-SCAPE runs, so the replication sits inside the tool's own noise floor rather than outside it.

the_cutoff_is_not_a_monotone_knob.observation: Loosening 0.20 -> 0.30 SPLIT 7,094 co-membership pairs while merging only 1,848. A threshold should not break co-memberships as it loosens.
the_cutoff_is_not_a_monotone_knob.mechanism: BiG-SCAPE swaps AP preference 0.0 for DENSE_PREFERENCE -5.0 when a connected component's density reaches 0.85, which makes it split less. Loosening the cutoff MERGES components, which LOWERS their density, which flips them out of the dense regime and makes AP split them more. At 0.20 there are components of 125 nodes at density 0.99 and 124 at 0.97; by 0.30 they have been absorbed into components of 598 at 0.39 and 296 at 0.34.
the_cutoff_is_not_a_monotone_knob.consequence: Raising the cutoff to reduce over-splitting can increase it. Do not treat bigscape_cutoffs as a dial from 'split' to 'merged'.

families_split_on_host_species_not_chemi.evidence: Pfam-domain Jaccard between families, whole region against the rule core only. Six of the nine closest pairs have IDENTICAL core domain content.
families_split_on_host_species_not_chemi.control: GCF-1 / GCF-16 -- Pantoea against Pectobacterium, a genuinely different chemistry -- has core Jaccard 0.167, so the core metric does discriminate real differences rather than calling everything identical.
families_split_on_host_species_not_chemi.why_it_happens: Median domains per record: 4 inside the rule core, 19 across the whole region. 79% of what BiG-SCAPE compares is flanking chromosomal context, which differs by host species.
families_split_on_host_species_not_chemi.persistence: The dense 13-family block (751 BGCs, GCF-1,2,7..18) goes 14 -> 13 -> 12 families as the cutoff goes 0.20 -> 0.30 -> 0.40. GCF-1 and GCF-2 stay separate at every cutoff despite representatives 0.020 apart.

neighbourhood.question: Could antismash_phosphonate_neighbourhood have been 8 rather than 10?
neighbourhood.answer: No. Measured over the 169 complete (non contig-edge) members of the pantaphos family, the distance from the rule core to the furthest downstream CDS is p0 9,189 / p50 9,318 / p95 9,451 / p100 9,792 bp. 8 kb and 9 kb both clip the terminal gene in every member; 10 kb clears the worst case by 208 bp.
neighbourhood.the_terminal_gene: An ATP-grasp domain protein wherever it is annotated -- the second ATP-grasp already recorded as missing at 5 kb.
neighbourhood.spread: 603 bp across 169 genomes, which is a conserved cluster boundary rather than arbitrary flanking DNA.
neighbourhood.is_10_kb_itself_clipping: No, on the one genome where it can be checked: at NEIGHBOURHOOD 20 on LMG 5342 the downstream flank beyond the cluster is 10.8 kb, so nothing lies past 9.2 kb.
neighbourhood.the_tension: 9.8 kb is required to capture the cassette, and ~10 kb of flank is what makes BiG-SCAPE split on species. Neither parameter resolves this alone.

what_this_does_not_settle: Whether a core-weighted or asymmetric comparison would cluster better was not tested; the ablation in CLAUDE.md's HGT section trimmed to core +/- 2 kb and got Jaccard 0.259 against control, so a naive trim is not the answer either.
Cutoffs above 0.40 were not swept. Given the density-flip mechanism they could go either way, and the sweep should be extended before anyone concludes 0.50 merges the block.

This reuses one run's distances. It therefore tests the CLUSTERING step at three cutoffs, not the whole pipeline at three cutoffs -- which is the right scope for this question, since the distances do not depend on the cutoff.

neighbourhood_8kb_experiment.status: SUPERSEDED by the asymmetric arm, but kept as the control. See where_the_cassette_actually_is. run_windows.sh runs sym8, asym and asym2 together.

what_is_already_measured.pantaphos: 8 kb clips the terminal ATP-grasp in every one of the 169 complete members, since the furthest downstream CDS sits 9,189-9,792 bp past the rule core. The cassette would be incomplete at 8 kb.

neighbourhood_8kb_experiment.method: trim_regions.py re-cuts the region GenBanks antiSMASH already produced at 10 kb to core +/- N, rather than re-running antiSMASH. Valid because detection does not move with the neighbourhood: the same 334 regions in the same 299 genomes were found at 5 kb and at 10 kb on Erwiniaceae. Verified on a 9-region sample: BiG-SCAPE's own parser accepts 9 of 9, with region, cand_cluster, protocluster and proto_core bounds correct including the contig-edge case where the window clamps at 0, and 3.67 CDS dropped per region against the 3 the database predicts.
neighbourhood_8kb_experiment.a_shortcut_that_does_not_work: Loading records from the finished database, narrowing each one's nt_start/nt_stop to core +/- 8 kb and calling BiG-SCAPE's comparison code on them would avoid the Pfam scan entirely. That comparison code is callable and exact -- it reproduced 60 of 60 stored distances -- but narrowing a record in place desynchronises the CDS indices its LCS extension walks, raising KeyError in score_extend_rev. The crash is the good outcome; the same inconsistency could have returned plausible wrong distances instead.
neighbourhood_8kb_experiment.what_it_will_and_will_not_settle: It gives the family structure at 8 kb against the 10 kb run at all three cutoffs. It does NOT make 8 kb a usable setting -- the terminal ATP-grasp is lost either way. The point is to measure how much of the species-splitting is attributable to the outer 2 kb, which bounds how much a core-weighted comparison could buy.

where_the_cassette_actually_is.finding: The phosphonate cassette lies ENTIRELY DOWNSTREAM of the rule core. Every upstream kilobase of the neighbourhood is divergent host context. So the window that would stop families splitting on species is ASYMMETRIC, not smaller -- a symmetric shrink to 8 kb is the worst of both, clipping the terminal ATP-grasp while still carrying 8 kb of the flank that splits them.
where_the_cassette_actually_is.method: For each 1 kb bin of offset from the rule core, the median Pfam-domain Jaccard between all cross-pairs of two families that BiG-SCAPE split. Shared content is cassette; divergent content is flank.
where_the_cassette_actually_is.orientation_matters_and_nearly_ruined_th: antiSMASH writes regions in CONTIG coordinates, so 91 of 186 pantaphos regions are reverse-complemented relative to the rest. The first run of this analysis did not normalise and produced a near-perfectly MIRRORED profile -- PF01048 at both -10 and +9, PF13535 at -9 and +8 -- which is a one-sided cluster smeared symmetric, not biology. Normalise on the strand of the pepM CDS (PF13714).
where_the_cassette_actually_is.a_second_trap: Conservation WITHIN a family does not separate cassette from flank. GCF-1 is 172 of 186 Pantoea ananatis, so its upstream flank is 80% conserved too -- deoD, penicillin-binding protein 2, a diguanylate cyclase. The test has to be what two SPLIT families share, not what one family conserves.
where_the_cassette_actually_is.the_proposal: Compare on core -0 / +10 kb. Keeps the entire cassette, so BGCs that differ in tailoring content still separate -- which is the point of having a neighbourhood at all -- while removing about half the window, all of it the divergent flank. Measured on a 9-region sample it drops 10.67 CDS per region against 3.67 for symmetric 8 kb: roughly 3x the flank removed, with no cassette loss.
where_the_cassette_actually_is.how_to_do_it: antiSMASH has no asymmetric neighbourhood option, and it does not need one -- this is a re-cut for COMPARISON only, so detection stays at 10 kb symmetric. trim_regions.py --up 0 --down 10 orients on pepM and emits GBKs BiG-SCAPE accepts (verified 9 of 9, both strands). run_windows.sh runs the symmetric and asymmetric arms side by side.
where_the_cassette_actually_is.status: PREPARED, NOT RUN -- still needs Pfam from the external drive.
